overview: The period was dominated by Alexei Starovoitov's landmark 49-patch series overhauling the BPF verifier to verify programs in multiple passes using an equation-based state representation — both the initial v1 posting and a quick v2 revision landed the same day. Alongside this, Tamir Duberstein posted v3 of a series fixing ring buffer issues and adding a caller-owned libbpf iterator, while Ihor Solodrai advanced support for kernel-side kfunc variants to v2.

patches.title: bpf: Verify in passes
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: The core patch in a 49-patch overhaul of the BPF verifier that introduces multi-pass verification with an equation-based state model. Instead of a single monolithic pass, the verifier now iterates over the program in passes, maintaining symbolic equations between registers so that inter-register relationships are preserved across joins and loops. This dramatically reduces false rejections of valid programs and replaces the old scalar evolution heuristic with a mathematically grounded approach. The series also rewrites verifier.rst to document the new algorithm.

patches.title: bpf: user_ringbuf: Handle position wrap
patches.author: Tamir Duberstein
patches.summary: First patch in an 8-patch series (v3) that fixes correctness bugs in BPF ring buffers and adds a new caller-owned iterator API in libbpf. This patch fixes a wrap-around bug in the user_ringbuf position calculation. The series also switches libbpf's ringbuf implementation to use compiler atomics, prevents missed wakeups on consumer wakeup, simplifies the iterator, and adds comprehensive selftests for ringbuf callback semantics.

patches.title: libbpf: Separate interfaces shared with in-tree tools
patches.author: Ihor Solodrai
patches.summary: Opening patch of a 6-patch v2 series adding kernel-side kfunc variant support to libbpf. The series enables libbpf to resolve kfunc calls by matching function prototypes when multiple kfunc variants (e.g. ___v2 suffixed names) exist for a given kernel version, allowing BPF programs to target the right variant automatically. It also updates sched_ext's compat.bpf.h to prefer ___v2 names and extends resolve_btfids to reject ambiguous variant registrations.

patches.title: libbpf: Fix CO-RE relocations of unsigned 32-bit enum values
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: v5 of a 3-patch series fixing a bug in libbpf's CO-RE relocation handling where unsigned 32-bit enum values were incorrectly sign-extended to 64 bits during relocation. This could cause incorrect enum comparisons in BPF programs loaded against kernels with differing enum layouts. The series also adds selftests for unsigned 32-bit enum relocations and for signed enum relocations of values lacking the kflag.

patches.title: bpf: Use an on-stack pt_regs in the raw tracepoint helpers
patches.author: Mike Bazov
patches.summary: v3 of a 3-patch series addressing preemption and nesting issues in BPF raw tracepoint helpers. This final patch switches bpf_perf_event_output() and related helpers to use an on-stack pt_regs copy rather than a per-CPU one, eliminating the need for preemption disabling in that path. The series also converts a WARN to a silent return when bpf_perf_event_output() nests too deep, and limits mmap_read_trylock() nesting in BPF helpers to prevent deadlocks.

patches.title: bpf, arm32: build constants inline instead of using a literal pool
patches.author: Ramin Moussavi
patches.summary: v2 patch improving the ARM32 BPF JIT to emit 32-bit constants inline using MOV/MOVT instruction pairs instead of loading them from a literal pool. This avoids PC-relative loads, reduces the JIT's reliance on the constant pool mechanism, and can improve instruction cache behavior for BPF programs on ARM32 targets. The change is a minor but clean optimization to the ARM32 JIT backend.

patches.title: selftests/bpf: Disable preemption around css_rstat_updated()
patches.author: Karl Mehltretter
patches.summary: Single-patch fix for a BPF selftest that calls css_rstat_updated() without holding the necessary preemption-disabled context. The function requires preemption to be disabled on some kernel configurations, and calling it from a context where preemption is enabled can trigger warnings or incorrect behavior. This patch wraps the call with preempt_disable/preempt_enable to satisfy that requirement.
